findings.body:
**Keep lifecycle scripts reached through opaque commands.**

If `prepare` runs `make bootstrap` and that Make target runs `npm run generate`, this branch returns an empty selection. `generate` is then omitted from the comparison. Changing its command can leave the worker using dependencies prepared with the old command. npm runs `prepare` during a local install. ([github.com](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/latest/docs/lib/content/using-npm/scripts.md?utm_source=openai))

Return unresolved for commands whose dispatch this parser does not model. Keep precise selection for explicit calls such as `npm run generate`.
findings.title: Keep lifecycle scripts reached through opaque commands.

findings.body:
**Keep workspace exclusions scoped to their package manager.**

If `pnpm-workspace.yaml` includes `packages/*` and `package.json` excludes `packages/cli`, the shared exclusion list drops `packages/cli` from the comparison. pnpm does not use the `package.json` workspace declaration. A change to that member's dependencies can therefore pass validation against a prepared pnpm tree for the old manifest. ([pnpm.io](https://pnpm.io/settings?utm_source=openai))

Apply each declaration's exclusions before combining the member sets, or enumerate only the workspace definition used to prepare the installed tree.
findings.title: Keep workspace exclusions scoped to their package manager.

findings.body:
**Compare pnpm resolution hooks before reusing dependencies.**

A change to `.pnpmfile.cjs` can change the version selected by `readPackage`. If the candidate still has the old lockfile, both metadata comparisons pass because neither checks the hook. The worker can then reuse a tree built with the old resolution. pnpm 10 loads this hook next to the lockfile. ([pnpm.io](https://pnpm.io/10.x/pnpmfile))

Compare the hook as bytes alongside the lockfile, including at member level where applicable. Keep reuse valid when the hook is absent from both roots.






Also applies to: 647-647
findings.title: Compare pnpm resolution hooks before reusing dependencies.

findings.body:
**Return the full script set on an unresolved selection.**

When many scripts contain shell expansions, each unresolved selection queues every unselected script again, including scripts already in `worklist`. With 20,000 such scripts, the loop can accumulate roughly 200 million queue entries without calling `admit`. That can exhaust the worker's heap before it reports a precondition failure.

Return all script names on the first unresolved selection. This gives the same result and avoids building the duplicate queue. Continue following explicit invocations and hooks for resolved selections.
findings.title: Return the full script set on an unresolved selection.

findings.body:
**Accept line breaks in NUL-delimited Git filenames.**

At `addressEvidence.ts:889`, `(.+)` rejects a tracked filename such as `docs/line\nbreak.txt`. Git emits the filename verbatim with `-z`. Even if that file is unchanged, the parser aborts settlement for a cancelled edit to another file. Parse the filename up to the NUL boundary without treating line breaks as record separators. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-ls-files.html?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Accept line breaks in NUL-delimited Git filenames.

findings.body:
**Record a created evidence ref before post-command validation can fail.**

If `update-ref` succeeds just before the cleanup deadline, `terminalGit` can reject during its post-command authority check. The collision probe also fails once authority expires. The ref exists, but `addressEvidence.ts:1014` never sets `attempt.retained`, so the lifecycle omits the ref from the report.

Record the successful ref update before the post-command check. Keep the authority check before restoration, so a late completion can be reported without allowing further writes.
findings.title: Record a created evidence ref before post-command validation can fail.

findings.body:
**Do not advertise a report that terminal cleanup skipped.**

If the journal directory is absent, `addressRunLifecycle.ts:479` skips the report write. Cleanup can still succeed, but Line 616 tells the operator to open a report that does not exist. Track whether persistence succeeded. Include the path when it did, and say that no report was written when cleanup intentionally skipped it.
findings.title: Do not advertise a report that terminal cleanup skipped.

findings.body:
**Preserve the ordinary report if terminal publication fails.**

At `addressEvidence.ts:1143`, the writer overwrites the verified ordinary report in place. If the filesystem accepts part of the new JSON and then returns an error, the old report can contain a new prefix and an old tail. The lifecycle reports the write failure but cannot recover the original report.

Stage and sync the new report before publishing it. Preserve the checked target identity and the exclusive-create rule for new reports.
findings.title: Preserve the ordinary report if terminal publication fails.

findings.body:
**Keep bookkeeping entries separate for each checkout root.**

`noteAddressTerminalBookkeeping` accepts a `root` argument but stores the bookkeeping map in one slot on the session. When one terminal session records bookkeeping for two checkouts, the second call discards the first checkout's entries. Settlement for the first checkout then finds no digest for its own bookkeeping file and fails with `terminal unknown untracked path`. Its failed-attempt evidence is not settled. The error keeps the caller's bytes, so no data is lost.

Registration for one root must not remove entries recorded for another root in the same session. The stored entries must stay addressable by checkout, so settlement for each root checks only its own bookkeeping files.
findings.title: Keep bookkeeping entries separate for each checkout root.
